preamble: Replacement of a glottal stop by the labio-velar glide [w] is attested in Tunisian Arabic of Nefza, where some verbs whose first root consonant was Old Arabic hamza (ʔ) now begin with w- in both perfect and imperfect and inflect like primae w verbs. The change is lexically restricted and regional.

examples.note: Pattern II verb with first radical ʔ; the hamza became w, so the verb now inflects as primae w.

examples.to: waxxaṛ – ywaxxaṛ 'to be late; to move backwards'
examples.note: Same development of first-radical ʔ to w in a pattern II verb.

sources: Naddari, A. (2024). The Arabic Variety of Nefza (Northwest Tunisia): Phonology, Morphology and Texts. Prensas de la Universidad de Zaragoza. https://zaguan.unizar.es/record/151519
